title: Identity vs. Structural Equality Ambiguity in Entities
damaged_code:
```rust
#[derive(PartialEq)]
struct UserEntity {
    id: u64,
    username: String,
    email: String, // email changing breaks equality!
}
```
pattern: Deriving or implementing structural equality (`PartialEq` comparing all fields) on an object that represents a domain Entity with a persistent identity.
why_bad: Entities are defined by a thread of continuity and identity, not their attributes. If a user changes their email, they are still the same physical user. Using structural equality means a modified entity is considered a different object, breaking collections, caches, and repository synchronization.
detection: A struct representing a domain Entity (possessing a unique ID field like `id` or `uuid`) that derives `PartialEq` or compares non-ID fields in its `eq` implementation.
counterexample:
A pure Value Object where structural equality is expected because it has no identity:
```rust
#[derive(PartialEq)]
struct FullName {
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
}
```
source: *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* by Vaughn Vernon (Chapter 5, p. 218); *Domain Modeling made Functional* by Scott Wlaschin (p. 92).
